met_analysis:
The Low-Pressure area oversoutheast Rajasthan & adjoining Madhya Pradesh lies over southeast Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 0830 Hrs IST of today, 24th July, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 9.4 km above mean sea level tilting south-westwards with height.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Jaisalmer, centre of Low-Pressure area over southeast Rajasthan & neighbourhood, Guna, Sidhi, Daltonganj & thence Southeastwards towards Northeast Bay of Bengal.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northern parts of Gangetic West Bengal & adjoining Bangladesh and now extends upto 9.4 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northwest Bay of Bengal & neighbourhood between 5.8 & 9.4 km above mean sea level merged with the above cyclonic circulation.
A trough runs from centre of Low-Pressure area over southeast Rajasthan & neighbourhood to Jammu across West Rajasthan, Haryana & Punjab between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 30°N persists A weak offshore trough at the mean sea level runs from Gujarat to Karnataka coast.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northeast Assam & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists. The east-west shear zone roughly along 23°N Lat. between 4.5 & 7.6 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
